questions.title: Structured Error Responses
questions.question: How do you design and implement consistent error responses in a REST API?

sections.title: What the Interviewer Wants to Hear
sections.content:
- **Consistent error response schema across all endpoints**
- **RFC 7807 Problem Details format — industry standard**
- **Include: status, error code, message, field errors for validation**
- **Never expose: stack traces, SQL errors, internal paths**
- **Include `requestId`: correlate frontend errors with backend logs**
- **Red flag:** different error formats per endpoint — clients can't parse errors uniformly

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
Consistent error responses are a fundamental API quality requirement. Every error, regardless of cause, should follow the same JSON structure so clients can parse errors uniformly. RFC 7807 defines a standard format — Problem Details for HTTP APIs — that includes `type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`, and optionally custom fields.

For validation errors, include field-level errors so clients can highlight the specific invalid fields. For business errors, include an `errorCode` that the frontend can map to user-friendly messages without relying on message text (which might change).

Never include internal details in error responses: stack traces, SQL queries, file paths, or exception class names. Log them on the server; return sanitized messages to clients. Always include a `requestId` or `correlationId` — when a user reports an error, you need to find the corresponding log entry.
